note: Externally-observable compliance checklist for a public domain. decision_mode routes each check: 'auto' = decided deterministically by evaluate.mjs from collected evidence; 'llm' = bounded judgment over the privacy-notice text (schema-validated); 'manual' = not observable from outside / requires interactive-browser or internal review.

checks.title: No non-essential cookies/trackers set before consent
checks.obligation: Storing or reading any non-strictly-necessary information on the user's device requires prior informed opt-in consent before that storage/access occurs.
checks.external_observable: Inspect Set-Cookie headers and client storage (cookies, localStorage, IndexedDB) on the very first HTTP response and initial page render, before any interaction with a consent UI.
signals: Set-Cookie with analytics/marketing cookie (_ga, _gid, _fbp, IDE, MUID) present on first response before consent
localStorage/IndexedDB keys for trackers written pre-consent
third-party tracker network requests fired on initial load before any click
checks.pass_criteria: Only strictly-necessary cookies (session, CSRF, load-balancing, consent-state) are present before the user makes a consent choice; all analytics/marketing storage is deferred until opt-in.
fail_indicators: _ga / _gid / _gat (Google Analytics) set before consent
_fbp or fr (Meta) set before consent
third-party marketing cookies present on landing with no interaction
tracker scripts execute network calls before consent click

checks.title: Cookie consent banner is present on first visit
checks.obligation: Before setting non-essential cookies the site must provide clear, comprehensive information and a means to give or refuse consent.
checks.external_observable: Detect a consent banner/CMP overlay rendered on first load for a fresh (cookieless) visitor.
signals: DOM element or iframe matching known CMP vendors (OneTrust, Cookiebot, Quantcast/TCF, Usercentrics, Didomi, CookieYes)
presence of __tcfapi / __cmp TCF API in window
visible banner text referencing cookies/consent
checks.pass_criteria: A consent banner or layer is shown on first visit and offers a real choice before non-essential processing.
fail_indicators: no banner at all while non-essential cookies are being set
banner only links to policy with no choice controls

checks.title: Reject-all available at first layer with equal prominence
checks.obligation: Refusing consent must be as easy as giving it; where an Accept-all is offered, an equally accessible Reject-all must be presented on the same layer.
checks.external_observable: Compare the buttons on the first banner layer: presence, label, size, colour/contrast and layer position of a Reject/Decline-all versus Accept-all.
signals: first-layer button labelled 'Reject all' / 'Decline' / 'Refuse'
Reject button at same DOM layer as Accept (no extra click into settings)
comparable styling/contrast between Accept and Reject
checks.pass_criteria: A Reject-all (or equivalent) is present on the first layer with prominence comparable to Accept-all.
fail_indicators: only 'Accept all' + 'Settings' on first layer, no first-layer reject
Reject hidden behind extra clicks
Reject rendered low-contrast/grey vs prominent coloured Accept

checks.title: No pre-ticked / pre-enabled non-essential consent toggles
checks.obligation: Consent requires a clear affirmative act; pre-ticked boxes, default-on toggles, silence or inactivity do not constitute valid consent.
checks.external_observable: Open the banner's granular/settings layer and inspect the default state of non-essential purpose toggles before any user action.
signals: checkbox/toggle for analytics or marketing rendered in 'on'/checked state by default
TCF purpose toggles defaulted to enabled
input[type=checkbox][checked] for non-essential categories
checks.pass_criteria: All non-essential category toggles default to OFF/unchecked; only strictly-necessary is on and locked.
fail_indicators: analytics toggle checked by default
marketing/advertising toggle on by default
'legitimate interest' sliders pre-enabled for non-essential vendors

checks.title: No cookie wall forcing consent for access
checks.obligation: Consent is not freely given if access to a service is conditioned on consent to non-essential processing (cookie walls).
checks.external_observable: Check whether content is blocked/inaccessible until Accept is clicked, with no equivalent non-consent path.
signals: full-page modal blocking all content with only an Accept action
page body hidden/scroll-locked until consent given
no usable site state after choosing Reject
checks.pass_criteria: Site content remains accessible after refusing non-essential cookies; no take-it-or-leave-it wall.
fail_indicators: content unreachable unless 'Accept' clicked
Reject leads to blank page or denial of access

checks.title: Consent withdrawal is as easy as giving consent
checks.obligation: Data subjects must be able to withdraw consent at any time, and withdrawal must be as easy as giving it.
checks.external_observable: Look for a persistent re-access control to the consent settings after the banner is dismissed (floating icon, footer link, 'Cookie settings').
signals: persistent 'Cookie settings'/'Manage cookies' link in footer
floating CMP widget/icon to reopen preferences
withdrawal reachable in same number of clicks as consent
checks.pass_criteria: A reachable, persistent mechanism to withdraw/modify consent exists after the initial choice.
fail_indicators: no way to reopen consent settings once banner dismissed
withdrawal requires emailing the company / multi-step hunt

checks.title: Banner gives granular per-purpose choice, not all-or-nothing
checks.obligation: Consent must be specific to each distinct processing purpose; bundled consent for multiple purposes is invalid.
checks.external_observable: Inspect whether the banner exposes separate controls for distinct purposes (analytics vs marketing vs personalisation) rather than a single Accept.
signals: separate toggles per purpose category in settings layer
TCF purpose list with individual controls
distinct consent for each processing purpose
checks.pass_criteria: Distinct, separately selectable consent options exist for each non-essential purpose category.
fail_indicators: single global Accept covering analytics+ads+personalisation with no granularity
purposes bundled with no opt-out per purpose

checks.title: Consent choice is honoured (no firing after Reject)
checks.obligation: After a user refuses, non-essential cookies/trackers must not be set or read.
checks.external_observable: Click Reject-all, then re-inspect cookies/storage and outbound network requests for tracker activity.
signals: no new analytics/marketing cookies after Reject
no tracker network requests to ad/analytics hosts post-Reject
consent-state cookie reflects refusal
checks.pass_criteria: No non-essential cookies set and no tracker calls made after the user chooses Reject.
fail_indicators: _ga / _fbp / ad cookies appear after clicking Reject
tracker beacons fire to google-analytics.com / facebook.net after refusal

checks.title: Privacy policy is present and reachable
checks.obligation: The controller must provide information about processing in a concise, transparent, intelligible and easily accessible form.
checks.external_observable: Find a linked, reachable privacy notice (footer link, /privacy, /privacy-policy, /datenschutz, /privacy-policy.html) returning HTTP 200.
signals: footer link text 'Privacy Policy'/'Privacy Notice'/'Datenschutz'/'Informativa privacy'
reachable /privacy or /privacy-policy URL (200)
link present on landing page within 1 click
checks.pass_criteria: A privacy notice is reachable from the homepage within one click and loads successfully.
fail_indicators: no privacy link anywhere
privacy link 404s or redirects to unrelated page
privacy buried beyond reasonable navigation

checks.title: Notice states controller identity and contact details
checks.obligation: The notice must identify the controller (and representative where applicable) and provide contact details.
checks.external_observable: Parse the privacy notice text for a named legal entity and contact details (postal address, email).
signals: named company/legal entity in notice
postal address present
controller contact email present
EU representative named where controller is non-EU
checks.pass_criteria: The notice clearly names the controller and provides at least one working contact channel.
fail_indicators: no identifiable controller entity
no contact details at all
non-EU controller with no Art. 27 representative listed

checks.title: Notice states purposes and legal basis of processing
checks.obligation: The notice must state the purposes of processing and the legal basis, and the legitimate interests pursued where Art. 6(1)(f) is relied upon.
checks.external_observable: Search the notice for stated purposes and an explicit legal basis per purpose; for legitimate interest, a description of the interest.
signals: explicit purposes enumerated (e.g. analytics, marketing, order fulfilment)
legal basis named per purpose (consent / contract / legitimate interest)
legitimate interest described where invoked
checks.pass_criteria: Each processing purpose has a stated legal basis; legitimate-interest reliance is explained.
fail_indicators: no legal basis stated
vague 'we process data to improve services' with no basis
legitimate interest claimed with no description

checks.title: Notice lists recipients / categories of recipients
checks.obligation: The notice must disclose the recipients or categories of recipients of the personal data.
checks.external_observable: Search the notice for named recipients or recipient categories (processors, ad networks, analytics providers, hosting).
signals: named third parties (e.g. Google, Meta, AWS, Stripe)
recipient categories listed (payment processors, analytics providers, hosting)
alignment between listed recipients and trackers actually observed loading
checks.pass_criteria: Recipients or recipient categories are disclosed and broadly consistent with observed third-party hosts.
fail_indicators: no recipients disclosed at all
trackers observed loading (e.g. facebook.net) that are nowhere mentioned in the notice

checks.title: Notice states retention period or criteria
checks.obligation: The notice must state the storage period or, if not possible, the criteria used to determine it.
checks.external_observable: Search the notice for explicit retention periods or stated criteria for determining them.
signals: stated retention duration (e.g. '24 months')
criteria for determining retention described
per-category retention table
checks.pass_criteria: Retention periods or determining criteria are stated. Note: the truthfulness of stated periods is not externally verifiable.
fail_indicators: no mention of retention/storage period at all
vague 'as long as necessary' with no criteria

checks.title: Notice enumerates data subject rights and complaint right
checks.obligation: The notice must inform of the rights of access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability, objection, the right to withdraw consent, and the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority.
checks.external_observable: Search the notice for enumerated data subject rights, withdrawal of consent, and the supervisory-authority complaint right.
signals: list of rights: access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability, objection
right to withdraw consent stated
right to lodge complaint with supervisory authority mentioned
checks.pass_criteria: All applicable rights, consent withdrawal, and the complaint right are described.
fail_indicators: no rights section
complaint-to-DPA right omitted
withdrawal-of-consent right omitted

checks.title: Notice uses clear, plain, accessible language
checks.obligation: Information must be concise, intelligible and in clear and plain language.
checks.external_observable: Assess the rendered notice for readability, layering/structure, and language matching the site's primary/targeted language.
signals: layered/structured notice with headings
notice language matches site audience language
absence of impenetrable legalese-only single block
checks.pass_criteria: The notice is structured, readable and in the audience's language.
fail_indicators: wall-of-text untranslated boilerplate in wrong language
no structure or headings making required info undiscoverable

checks.title: Cookie/tracker disclosure exists and matches reality
checks.obligation: Users must be given clear and comprehensive information about cookies/trackers, their purposes and duration.
checks.external_observable: Compare a cookie/tracker disclosure (cookie policy or CMP list) against the cookies/hosts actually observed.
signals: dedicated cookie policy or in-CMP cookie list
named cookies with purpose and duration
consistency between declared and actually-set cookies
checks.pass_criteria: A cookie disclosure exists and substantially matches the cookies/trackers actually observed.
fail_indicators: cookies set with no disclosure anywhere
declared list omits trackers observed loading (e.g. undisclosed fingerprinting/pixels)

checks.title: A lawful basis is stated for each processing purpose
checks.obligation: Processing must rest on at least one of the six lawful bases in Art. 6(1), and the basis must be communicated.
checks.external_observable: Read the privacy notice for an explicit Art. 6(1) basis mapped to each stated purpose.
signals: basis named per purpose (consent, contract, legal obligation, legitimate interest, etc.)
consent used as basis for marketing/analytics
legitimate-interest balancing referenced where relied on
checks.pass_criteria: Every stated purpose has a declared lawful basis. Substantive correctness of the basis is not externally verifiable.
fail_indicators: no lawful basis stated for any purpose
consent claimed as basis while cookies fire before consent (basis contradicted by behaviour)

checks.title: Consent-based processing is backed by valid consent mechanics
checks.obligation: Where consent is the basis, it must be freely given, specific, informed, unambiguous and demonstrable.
checks.external_observable: Cross-check declared consent basis against observed banner behaviour (opt-in, granularity, pre-consent firing).
signals: banner mechanics consistent with claimed consent basis
no pre-consent firing where consent is the declared basis
demonstrable opt-in flow
checks.pass_criteria: Observed consent UI mechanics are consistent with a valid Art. 4(11)/Art. 7 consent.
fail_indicators: notice claims consent basis but trackers fire pre-consent
consent basis claimed with pre-ticked toggles or no reject option

checks.title: Accessible channel to exercise data subject rights
checks.obligation: The controller must facilitate the exercise of data subject rights and provide a means to make such requests.
checks.external_observable: Locate a request channel in the notice (privacy/DSR email, web form, postal address, rights-request page).
signals: privacy@ or dpo@ email for requests
dedicated DSR/'manage my data' web form
postal address for written requests
instructions on how to exercise each right
checks.pass_criteria: At least one concrete, reachable channel for exercising rights is provided.
fail_indicators: no contact method for rights requests
generic sales contact only with no privacy channel

checks.title: Right to object to direct marketing is offered
checks.obligation: Data subjects have an absolute right to object to processing for direct marketing, and must be informed of it explicitly.
checks.external_observable: Check the notice and any marketing sign-up flow for an explicit opt-out/objection to direct marketing and unsubscribe mechanics.
signals: explicit 'object to marketing' / opt-out statement
newsletter sign-up presents unsubscribe info
marketing consent separable from other processing
checks.pass_criteria: The right to object to direct marketing is clearly offered and explained.
fail_indicators: no marketing objection/opt-out mentioned
marketing bundled with no separate opt-out

checks.title: Disclosure of automated decision-making / profiling
checks.obligation: Where solely automated decisions with legal/similar effect exist, the controller must disclose this and provide meaningful information about the logic involved.
checks.external_observable: Search the notice for any statement on automated decision-making or profiling and accompanying logic explanation.
signals: section on automated decision-making/profiling
meaningful information about the logic
statement of significance/consequences for the data subject
checks.pass_criteria: If profiling/ADM is used it is disclosed with logic explained; absence of such processing is also acceptable. Whether ADM actually occurs is not externally verifiable.
fail_indicators: evident profiling features (e.g. personalised pricing signals) with no ADM disclosure

checks.title: Site served over valid HTTPS with modern TLS
checks.obligation: The controller must implement technical measures appropriate to risk to ensure confidentiality and integrity of personal data in transit.
checks.external_observable: Perform a TLS handshake and certificate validation; check protocol version and cipher strength.
signals: valid, non-expired, trusted certificate
TLS >= 1.2 (ideally 1.3) negotiated
no support for SSLv3/TLS 1.0/1.1
strong cipher suites only
checks.pass_criteria: Valid certificate and TLS 1.2+ with strong ciphers; no deprecated protocols.
fail_indicators: expired/self-signed/untrusted certificate
TLS 1.0/1.1 or SSLv3 supported
site reachable over plain HTTP serving forms

checks.title: HTTP redirects to HTTPS and HSTS is set
checks.obligation: Appropriate measures should enforce encrypted transport to protect personal data integrity and confidentiality.
checks.external_observable: Request the HTTP (port 80) URL and inspect for redirect to HTTPS; inspect response headers for Strict-Transport-Security.
signals: HTTP 301/308 redirect to https://
Strict-Transport-Security header present with reasonable max-age
includeSubDomains / preload where appropriate
checks.pass_criteria: HTTP redirects to HTTPS and an HSTS header is present.
fail_indicators: plain HTTP served without redirect
no HSTS header
mixed-content resources loaded over HTTP

checks.title: Forms collecting personal data submit securely
checks.obligation: Personal data collected via forms must be transmitted with appropriate security (encrypted transport).
checks.external_observable: Inspect form action targets and page transport for login/contact/checkout/registration forms.
signals: form action posts to an https:// endpoint
no personal-data form on a plain-HTTP page
no form action to a third-party host inconsistent with the notice
checks.pass_criteria: All personal-data-collecting forms post over HTTPS to disclosed endpoints.
fail_indicators: form posts over HTTP
password/payment form on insecure page
undisclosed third-party form endpoint capturing PII

checks.title: Security-hardening response headers present
checks.obligation: State-of-the-art technical measures appropriate to risk should be applied to reduce data-exposure risks.
checks.external_observable: Inspect HTTP response headers for common hardening directives.
signals: Content-Security-Policy present
X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
Referrer-Policy restricting referrer leakage
X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors anti-clickjacking
no Server/X-Powered-By version leakage
checks.pass_criteria: A reasonable set of hardening headers is present (CSP, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, anti-clickjacking).
fail_indicators: no security headers at all
verbose version-disclosing Server headers
Referrer-Policy leaking full URLs to third parties

checks.title: Enumerate third-party tracking hosts loaded
checks.obligation: Embedding third-party content that transmits user data makes the operator a joint controller and requires a lawful basis/consent and disclosure.
checks.external_observable: Capture all outbound network requests and classify third-party hosts by category (analytics, advertising, social, CDN, tag managers).
signals: third-party hosts loaded: google-analytics.com, googletagmanager.com, facebook.net, doubleclick.net, hotjar.com, etc.
tag manager containers present
social plugins/SDKs loaded
checks.pass_criteria: All third-party trackers are inventoried; non-essential ones load only after consent and are disclosed.
fail_indicators: advertising/analytics third parties loading on first paint pre-consent
trackers present but undisclosed in the notice

checks.title: Social plugins / embeds do not transmit data before consent
checks.obligation: Social plugins (Like buttons, embedded video/maps) create joint controllership and must not transmit personal data before a lawful basis/consent exists.
checks.external_observable: Detect embedded social/third-party widgets and check whether they call home before any consent.
signals: Facebook Like/SDK, X/Twitter widgets, YouTube/Vimeo embeds, Google Maps iframes firing on load
requests carrying cookies/IP to social hosts pre-consent
absence of click-to-load / consent gating for embeds
checks.pass_criteria: Social/third-party embeds are consent-gated (e.g. click-to-load) and do not transmit data pre-consent.
fail_indicators: Like button or YouTube embed sends data to third party on first load before consent
Google Maps/embed loads cookies pre-consent

checks.title: No covert device fingerprinting before consent
checks.obligation: Fingerprinting that reads/stores information on the device falls under Art. 5(3) and requires consent unless strictly necessary.
checks.external_observable: Detect fingerprinting techniques executing before consent (canvas/WebGL/font enumeration, audio fingerprinting, aggressive device-attribute reads).
signals: canvas/WebGL fingerprinting scripts running pre-consent
known fingerprinting libraries (FingerprintJS) loaded
extensive navigator/device probing before any consent
checks.pass_criteria: No non-essential fingerprinting occurs before consent.
fail_indicators: canvas/audio fingerprinting executed on first load
FingerprintJS or similar active pre-consent

checks.title: Detect likely third-country transfers via tracker geography
checks.obligation: Transfers of personal data to third countries require an adequacy decision, appropriate safeguards (SCCs/BCRs), or a derogation.
checks.external_observable: Map loaded third-party hosts and resolved IP/CDN geography to infer transfers to non-EEA recipients (notably US ad/analytics providers).
signals: data sent to US-based hosts (google-analytics.com, facebook.net, doubleclick.net)
IP geolocation/ASN of endpoints outside EEA
non-EEA tag/CDN endpoints receiving identifiers
checks.pass_criteria: Any inferred transfer is to a recipient covered by adequacy (e.g. DPF-certified US org) or backed by safeguards described in the notice.
fail_indicators: personal data sent to non-EEA trackers with no transfer disclosure
US trackers fire pre-consent with no transfer mechanism stated

checks.title: Notice discloses transfers and safeguards (SCC/DPF/adequacy)
checks.obligation: Where data is transferred to a third country, the notice must reference the safeguards (e.g. SCCs, DPF/adequacy) and how to obtain a copy.
checks.external_observable: Search the notice for international-transfer disclosure and named transfer mechanisms.
signals: mention of transfers outside EEA
named mechanism: adequacy decision / EU-US Data Privacy Framework / Standard Contractual Clauses / BCRs
statement on how to obtain SCC copy
checks.pass_criteria: Transfers are disclosed with a valid named safeguard consistent with the trackers observed. Whether SCCs/TIA actually exist is not externally verifiable.
fail_indicators: US recipients observed loading but notice silent on transfers
transfers mentioned with no mechanism named
reliance on invalidated Privacy Shield language

checks.title: Children's consent / age handling where service targets minors
checks.obligation: For information society services offered to children, consent must be given or authorised by a parent below the applicable age (16, or as low as 13 by member-state law).
checks.external_observable: Assess whether the site is directed at children (theme, content, language) and whether any age-gate or parental-consent mechanism exists at sign-up.
signals: child-oriented content/branding/games
age-gate or date-of-birth field at registration
parental-consent step where minors targeted
absence of marketing trackers on child-directed pages
checks.pass_criteria: If the service is directed at or likely used by children, an age-verification / parental-consent mechanism is present.
fail_indicators: evidently child-directed service with no age gate and consent-based marketing trackers
no age handling on a kids' product

checks.title: Child-comprehensible transparency where minors targeted
checks.obligation: Information addressed to a child must be in clear and plain language the child can easily understand.
checks.external_observable: On child-directed pages, assess whether privacy information is presented in age-appropriate language.
signals: simplified/child-friendly privacy explanation on kids' pages
age-appropriate consent prompts
checks.pass_criteria: Child-directed services present age-appropriate transparency.
fail_indicators: only dense adult legalese on a clearly child-directed service

checks.title: DPO contact details published where a DPO is required
checks.obligation: Where a DPO is designated, the controller must publish and communicate the DPO's contact details.
checks.external_observable: Search the notice/site for DPO contact details (dpo@ email, named DPO, postal contact).
signals: dpo@domain email
named Data Protection Officer
DPO postal/contact section in notice
checks.pass_criteria: DPO contact details are published where a DPO is required. Whether a DPO is legally required depends on internal processing facts not externally verifiable.
fail_indicators: large-scale/sensitive processing evident but no DPO contact anywhere
notice refers to a DPO with no contact details

checks.title: EU representative published for non-EU controllers
checks.obligation: A controller not established in the EU but targeting EU data subjects must designate and publish an EU representative.
checks.external_observable: Determine apparent establishment (entity address, hosting, targeting) and search the notice for a named Art. 27 EU representative.
signals: named EU representative with EEA address in notice
controller entity located outside EEA while targeting EU users
representative contact channel listed
checks.pass_criteria: Non-EU controllers targeting the EU name an EU representative. Establishment status is only inferable, not certain.
fail_indicators: clearly non-EU controller targeting EU users with no Art. 27 representative listed

checks.title: Records of processing (Art. 30) — internal, not observable
checks.obligation: Controllers/processors must maintain internal records of processing activities.
checks.external_observable: Not externally observable. Existence and adequacy of ROPA can only be confirmed by internal documentation review or a supervisory authority request.
signals: N/A from outside — requires manual/internal review of the controller's records
checks.pass_criteria: Flagged for manual/internal audit; cannot be passed or failed from external observation alone.
fail_indicators: none externally observable

checks.title: DPIA (Art. 35) — internal, not observable
checks.obligation: A data protection impact assessment is required for high-risk processing.
checks.external_observable: Not externally observable. Whether a DPIA was performed for high-risk processing requires internal documentation review.
signals: N/A from outside — manual/internal review required; high-risk processing may be inferred but DPIA existence cannot
checks.pass_criteria: Flagged for manual/internal audit; cannot be judged from external observation alone.
fail_indicators: none externally observable

checks.title: Processor contracts (Art. 28) — internal, not observable
checks.obligation: Engaging a processor requires a binding contract with the Art. 28(3) mandatory terms.
checks.external_observable: Not externally observable. Third-party processors can be inferred from loaded hosts, but the existence/adequacy of DPAs requires internal contract review.
signals: N/A from outside — processors inferable from trackers, but contracts require internal review
checks.pass_criteria: Flagged for manual/internal audit; cannot be passed externally.
fail_indicators: none externally observable

checks.title: Breach notification process (Art. 33/34) — internal, not observable
checks.obligation: Controllers must notify the supervisory authority within 72 hours and, where high-risk, the affected data subjects.
checks.external_observable: Not externally observable. Breach-handling readiness/procedures require internal review; only publicly disclosed past breaches may occasionally be visible.
signals: N/A from outside — internal process review required; historical public breach disclosures may exist
checks.pass_criteria: Flagged for manual/internal audit; cannot be judged from external observation alone.
fail_indicators: none externally observable (beyond any public record of an unhandled past breach)

checks.title: No visual nudging steering toward Accept
checks.obligation: Consent must be freely given; interfaces must not deceptively steer users toward consenting (deceptive design / dark patterns).
checks.external_observable: Compare the visual treatment (colour, contrast, size, emphasis) of Accept vs Reject controls on the banner.
signals: Accept highlighted in bright/high-contrast colour while Reject is greyed/low-contrast
Accept large vs Reject tiny or text-only link
emphasis/animation directing to Accept
checks.pass_criteria: Accept and Reject have visually comparable, non-manipulative prominence.
fail_indicators: bright green Accept vs faint grey Reject
Reject reduced to a small text link beside a big Accept button

checks.title: No confusing/double-negative or misleading consent wording
checks.obligation: Consent requests must use clear, plain language and must not confuse or mislead the user about the effect of their choice.
checks.external_observable: Read banner/settings copy for confusing wording, double negatives, or misleading framing of the choice.
signals: double-negative toggles ('do not not collect')
ambiguous button labels ('OK' / 'Got it' that imply acceptance)
misleading framing of refusal consequences
checks.pass_criteria: Consent wording is clear, unambiguous and not misleading.
fail_indicators: only an 'OK/Got it' button implying consent with no real choice
double negatives or confusing toggle labels

checks.title: No nagging / repeated re-prompting after refusal
checks.obligation: Repeatedly re-prompting users who have refused, to pressure consent, undermines the freely-given requirement (the 'nagging' dark pattern).
checks.external_observable: After choosing Reject, navigate the site and reload to see whether the banner reappears persistently demanding consent.
signals: banner re-appears on every page load after a clear refusal
refusal not persisted (no consent-state cookie honoured)
repeated interstitials re-asking for consent
checks.pass_criteria: A refusal is persisted for a reasonable period without immediate re-nagging on each page.
fail_indicators: banner reappears every navigation after Reject
refusal state not stored, forcing repeated choices
